A maths book that calculates with you

Make the rectangles under a curve narrower and narrower until the sum turns into an integral, and turn a graph about the $x$-axis in real 3D until a cone, a sphere or a barrel appears. Lay the bell curve over a binomial histogram, toss a coin a thousand times to check whether it is biased, and look for the shortest connection between two skew lines. On top of that: proofs for the advanced course, exercises at three levels, self-checks with instant feedback and a whole chapter of training for the Abitur.

CONTENTSIN THE ORDER OF THE SCHOOL YEAR

The chapters follow the teaching plan of the advanced course in Year 12: first integral calculus with solids of revolution (learning area 5) until the autumn holidays, then the elective area numerical integration and normally distributed random variables (learning area 6) until the first exam, and in December inferential statistics (learning area 7). In the second half of the year come distances and angles in space with the Hesse normal form and skew lines (learning area 8) and the connected applications with extreme values, reflections, unbounded areas and families (learning area 9). In April you train for the Abitur. On the right you can see when each chapter is due and how many self-checks you have already solved.

HOW TO USE THIS BOOK
EVERY CHAPTER HAS THE SAME STRUCTURE
  1. Opener with learning goals and a check-in: what you should already be able to do.
  2. Explorations: open questions to try out, ideally in groups.
  3. Units: starter, explanation, key-point box, examples, interactive elements, exercises and “Test yourself!”.
  4. Review · Deepen · Connect: mixed exercises.
  5. Excursion: history, an application or a nice puzzle.
  6. Looking back on one page and a test with two rounds.
THE SYMBOLS

Basic   Intermediate   Advanced

Every exercise has the solution to fold out, some also a hint. Try it yourself first.

In the self-checks you type in your result. Fractions ($3/10$), decimals ($0.3$) and percentages ($30\%$) are all understood. Your browser remembers what you have solved.

Labs open in a new tab. There you can experiment for longer and more freely than in the book. The labs and the weekly exercise sheets are in German for now.

KEY POINT

Whatever is in an orange box, you need to know. Everything else helps you to understand it.
